overview: A wet Pacific Northwest pattern runs through the week. Systems keep arriving from the Pacific, with the strongest one due Wednesday into Thursday, bringing heavy rain and mountain snow to the Cascades and the Coast Mountains.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler has the most snow in this region, with 36 inches expected through Friday, and its biggest day is Wednesday at 11 inches. Snow levels are high, so the early Monday snow is the best of it, and rain is expected to mix in midweek. Cypress Mountain, with 13 inches, is more exposed to showers and rain, which could keep its snow-line lower.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Crystal Mountain has the most snow here, 20 inches through Friday, with its biggest day Thursday at 10 inches. Snow levels sit near 3,000 to 3,500 feet, and a stronger front Tuesday into Wednesday brings mountain snow and breezy winds. Winter Weather Advisory covers the Olympics through Monday afternoon.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
